items.q: What is Galpin's core training thesis?
items.a: **Concepts are few, methods are many.** Exercise choice does not determine adaptation — **modifiable variables** (sets, reps, intensity, rest, frequency) do. Train the outcome you want; fat loss is a byproduct.

items.q: What are the nine trainable adaptations?
items.a: **Skill, speed, power, strength, hypertrophy, muscular endurance, anaerobic power, VO2 max, and long-duration endurance.** Pushing one hard can sacrifice another.

**3–5 exercises × 3–5 reps × 3–5 sets × 3–5 min rest × 3–5 days/week** at **85%+ 1RM** for strength. Power uses the same structure at **40–70%** with velocity emphasis. Scales from ~**20 min/week** minimal to full five-day programs.
**Strength: intensity drives** (min ~**2×/week** per muscle). **Hypertrophy: volume drives** — **5–30 reps** per set to near failure; all ranges work if close to failure. More soreness ≠ more growth.

items.q: How should your mental focus differ by goal?
items.a: **Mind-muscle intentionality**: move the weight as a system for **strength**; challenge the **target muscle** for hypertrophy. Programming is "idiot-proof"; execution is hard.

items.q: What endurance work should sit in a typical week?
items.a: **150–180 min zone 2** (conversational; does not block hypertrophy), **once/week VO2-max touch** (4–8 bouts of ~**90 sec** near max HR; every other week minimum), plus **2–6 min hard repeats** at ~**80% HR**.

items.q: Why start endurance on bike/row/sled instead of running?
items.a: Start **concentric-dominant** modalities to avoid **eccentric soreness** from jumping into running. Zone 2 may even help hypertrophy via blood flow; HIIT complements, it doesn't replace.

items.q: What does "point of physiological failure" tell you?
items.a: Where you quit — **legs vs lungs** — reveals what to train next. Same VO2 max can mask different limiters. After hard intervals, do **3+ min exhale-emphasis breathing** to down-regulate.

items.q: What is the Galpin hydration equation?
items.a: **Body weight (lb) ÷ 30 = oz fluid per 15 min** of exercise/cognition. In heat or long sessions, add about **~1 g sodium per liter** of sweat.

items.q: When does cold help vs hurt adaptation?
items.a: Cold **blunts hypertrophy** if overused during growth blocks — use **pre-training** or **4+ hours away**. Morning cold can improve HRV; post-lift **sauna** may plausibly aid hypertrophy.

items.q: Which supplement does Galpin call the "Michael Jordan"?
items.a: **Creatine monohydrate** — strong safety profile, benefits beyond muscle, **~5 g/day** for most. Also discussed: sodium bicarbonate and beta-alanine.
